source_name: KIESA — Kosovo Exporters Directory (Ministry of Industry/Investment agency)
why_relevant: State-run exporters directory lists Kosovo ICT firms with self-declared capabilities and references; combined with STIKK it completes the local vendor/integrator actor map for supply-side monitoring.

source_name: MAPL - Portal opstina (Ministry of Local Government Administration municipality portal, Serbian version)
why_relevant: Authoritative pointer/index giving the official website of every Kosovo municipality, including the Serb-majority ones, in Serbian. Snowball entry point to 10 municipal procurement sections; MAPL also publishes legality-review (shqyrtimi i ligjshmerise) pages per municipality that can expose contested municipal decisions incl. financial ones.

source_name: Contracting-authority mirror pages (e.g. Dogana e Kosovës notice files, Ministry of Health OSHP decision files)
why_relevant: Individual Kosovo authorities mirror their own B08 award notices as PDFs in predictable shared folders. These mirrors are often reachable and indexable when the central portal's document application is behind login, giving a fallback retrieval route for specific notices (customs, tax administration, ministries — all buyers of payment and cash-handling services).

source_name: E-Prokurimi (KRPP central portal) — legislation & forms library
why_relevant: Not a substitute for the central portal itself (out of this cell), but its legislation library defines the standard forms (B05 contract notice, B08 award notice) and the publication thresholds — including that prior notices become mandatory for service contracts at/above EUR 500,000. That is the parsing schema and the filtering rule for every authority-level PDF collected in this cell. Serbian-language versions of the same instructions exist, confirming an official sr track.

source_name: kk.rks-gov.net municipal template — /<komuna>/category/prokurimi/ (all 38 municipalities)
why_relevant: Confirmed that Kosovo municipalities share a common CMS path pattern under kk.rks-gov.net (observed for Skenderaj and Prishtinë). This is the highest-leverage pointer in the cell: one URL template enumerates the procurement pages of ~38 contracting authorities, the densest population of low-visibility banking-services tenders.

source_name: AIP legacy archive subsite (aip.rks-gov.net/arkiva) — historical audit and institutional PDFs
why_relevant: A concrete example of a Kosovo government institution keeping an explicit /arkiva/ subtree containing older publications, including a 2017 audit report on financial statements. This is precisely the removed-but-preserved layer this cell targets, and the path structure (/arkiva/assets/cms/uploads/files/Publikime/) is a reusable fingerprint: probing for /arkiva/ across rks-gov.net institutional subdomains is a cheap, high-yield discovery tactic for recovering documents dropped from current site navigation.

source_name: STIKK — Shoqata e TIK e Kosovës, member directory
why_relevant: The ICT association member directory is the candidate-supplier universe for banking/payments IT tenders: system integrators and distributors that actually bid (CACTTUS, Kosbit, ITD Prishtinë, StarLabs, Ericsson Nikola Tesla branch, BIT Kosova, Panamic ICT). Each member page carries capabilities and vendor authorisations useful for competitor mapping.

source_name: STIKK — Kosovo ICT Association member directory
why_relevant: Highest-value pointer for this cell: ~100+ Kosovo ICT companies, including the local integrators and resellers who actually sign bank contracts (Asseco SEE Kosovo, Cacttus, LinkPlus IT, Panamic ICT and others). Snowballing the directory yields the vendor set whose own sites/press must then be monitored for Kosovo bank wins.

source_name: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës / Kosovo Banking Association (KBA)
why_relevant: Sector association founded 2002; its member list is the standard shorthand enumeration of commercial banks in Kosovo, and the association also publishes sector positions and events that reveal joint infrastructure projects (cards, instant payments) preceding tenders.

source_name: Balkan Tender Watch (regional CSO coalition)
why_relevant: Regional anti-corruption coalition (since 2012; members include Kosovo Foundation for Open Society, Open Society Serbia, OSF BiH, CCC North Macedonia) that publishes shadow reports on Kosovo public procurement, benchmarking tools and monitoring manuals. Its documents name the local monitoring NGOs, portals and recurring problem categories — a directory of where further Kosovo procurement sources live.

source_name: Media Ownership Monitor Kosovo - Serbian-language outlet registry
why_relevant: Systematic registry of Kosovo media outlets with ownership, reach and language - the fastest way to enumerate ALL Serbian-language outlets in Kosovo (not just the well-known ones) and to judge their independence/credibility before adding them to a monitoring list.

source_name: Gracanica Online (Omonia)
why_relevant: Serbian-language web portal covering political, social and ECONOMIC issues from Kosovo, based in the Gracanica enclave. Economic desk makes it more likely than pure-news outlets to cover municipal contracts and banking access. Record here is the Media Ownership Monitor profile (ownership + own-site details); the outlet's own domain should be resolved from it rather than guessed.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership — Kosovo transparency case study
why_relevant: Explains how the Kosovo OCDS publication was built, who the civil-society consumers are, and what the known data gaps are. This is the fastest snowball hub from the platform to the whole downstream ecosystem (prokurimihapur, redflags, Democracy Plus, Open Data Kosovo).

source_name: Open Data Kosovo — Open Businesses (scraped ARBK dataset, 170k+ businesses)
why_relevant: Civic-tech dataset explicitly built to link business registration data with public procurement and asset declarations — exactly the join needed to go from an award notice to a company profile and its owners.

source_name: Open Data Kosovo — e-Prokurimi project and red-flag dataset work
why_relevant: Open Data Kosovo has worked with municipalities to collect and visualise their procurement data into the e-prokurimi platform and built a red-flag algorithm that automatically detects irregularities in procurement processes. As a pointer this is valuable in two ways: it identifies which municipalities have digitised historical records at all (a coverage map for the archival layer), and any published red-flag dataset or codebook is a reusable scoring methodology for a market-intelligence pipeline.

source_name: AmCham Kosovo — Membership Directory
why_relevant: Well-structured, browsable directory (alphabetical and by category, incl. Patron Members) that reliably enumerates banks, payment/fintech firms and IT vendors active in Kosovo — one of the cleanest scrapable actor lists in the market.

source_name: AMIK — Shoqata e Institucioneve Mikrofinanciare të Kosovës, Anëtarët e AMIK
why_relevant: Enumerates the microfinance/NBFI segment (KEP Trust, KRK, AFK, Kos Invest and others) — a second tier of financial buyers that procure core banking, lending and payment systems and are easily missed if only banks are tracked.

source_name: AppsRunTheWorld — customer technographics profiles for Kosovo banks
why_relevant: Aggregator that maps named institutions to the software vendors they buy from. Profiles exist for Raiffeisen Bank Kosova and ProCredit Bank Kosovo, so it acts as a pointer telling you which vendor's newsroom/reference pages to go hunt for the underlying contract.

source_name: BKS — Byroja Kosovare e Sigurimit / Shoqata e Sigurimeve të Kosovës
why_relevant: Insurance bureau/association covering ~14 insurers (12 non-life, 2 life) with mixed domestic/Austrian/Albanian/Slovenian capital. Insurers are adjacent buyers of payment, claims and IT systems, and BKS itself runs sector infrastructure that gets tendered.

entity_name: CBK / Wikipedia consolidated list of licensed banks in Kosovo
source_name: CBK / Wikipedia consolidated list of licensed banks in Kosovo (actor map anchor)
why_relevant: Recurring anchor across every query in this cell; enumerates the full licensed set (ProCredit, Raiffeisen, NLB, TEB, BKT, BpB, Banka Ekonomike, Ziraat, Türkiye İş Bankası, PriBank) so no private buyer is missed when building the per-bank tender-page crawl list. The authoritative version is the CBK register, which this mirrors.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet Kosovo company profiles (vendor local entities)
why_relevant: Confirms which international banking-technology vendors have registered Kosovo entities (PRINTEC L.L.C. Prishtinë, ASSECO SEE SH.P.K.), giving exact legal names to match against procurement award notices and business-registry filings — the bridge between the supply-side and the tender-side workstream.

source_name: FSDK — Fondi i Sigurimit të Depozitave në Kosovë, Bankat Anëtare
why_relevant: Statutory deposit-insurance membership is compulsory for licensed banks, so this list is an independent cross-check on the BQK bank universe and updates when a bank enters/exits. FSDK itself is also a small contracting authority (IT/DRC projects).

source_name: FWC SEA 2023 — Framework Contract Services for the EU's External Action (successor to FWC SIEA 2018)
why_relevant: Most short/medium EU technical assistance in Kosovo (including financial sector, PFM and digital payments advisory) is contracted through FWC lots rather than open tenders, so the framework lot holders are the de-facto pre-selected supplier pool. Lot 8 (Sustainable Finance) and the ICT/digital lots are the relevant cells.

source_name: ICT Kosovo company directory (ictkosovo.eu)
why_relevant: Second, independent Kosovo ICT company registry (donor/cluster-run). Useful to cross-check STIKK and catch vendors not in STIKK; entries carry company profiles and reference claims that can reveal bank clients.

source_name: NVO Aktiv (Mitrovica North) - Serb-community governance watchdog
why_relevant: Leading Serb-community research NGO on institutions and governance in Kosovo; a pointer to Serbian-language actor names, municipal spending research and community-level access-to-finance issues. Note it has itself been the subject of political targeting, so treat framing carefully.

source_name: OCCRP Aleph — Kosovo Business Registration Agency dataset
why_relevant: Investigative-grade indexed copy of ARBK data, searchable by person as well as company — helps expose beneficial owners and directors linking suppliers to bank/public-sector counterparts.

source_name: Oda Ekonomike e Kosovës (OEK) — Kosovo Chamber of Commerce
why_relevant: Statutory chamber founded 1962 (Law No. 2004/7) with sectoral departments; its membership and sector-council composition enumerate mid-size Kosovar firms including IT and services suppliers, and its export/investment department publishes company listings.

source_name: OEGJK / KDWV — Oda Ekonomike Gjermano-Kosovare, Lista e plotë e anëtarëve
why_relevant: German-Kosovar chamber with ~200 members and an explicitly published full member list (including a downloadable member-company document) — a compact enumeration of firms with EU vendor ties, likely bidders/partners on banking IT projects.

source_name: OpenCorporates — Kosovo Business Registration Agency jurisdiction page
why_relevant: Normalised, queryable copy of Kosovo company records with stable identifiers; useful for cross-border ownership tracing of bidders (Turkish, Slovenian, Austrian, Albanian parents are common in XK banking/IT).

source_name: PaymentProviders.io — Kosovo country directory of payment providers
why_relevant: Commercial directory listing providers claiming Kosovo coverage; useful only as a name-generation seed for the actor map, since inclusion is not evidence of a BQK licence.

source_name: Privredna komora Kosova i Metohije (Serbian-language chamber, Kosovska Mitrovica)
why_relevant: The only Serbian-language chamber structure covering Serb-majority municipalities in Kosovo; enumerates firms that operate under the parallel/Serbian system and would otherwise be invisible in ARBK-only actor maps. Its links page points onward to Serbian registers (APR) relevant for cross-registered entities.

source_name: Shkabaj.net (Albanian-language Kosovo news aggregator)
why_relevant: Aggregator/start page linking the full spread of Albanian-language Kosovo and diaspora outlets. Its outbound link list is a cheap way to enumerate second- and third-tier sq portals that no single search will surface, and to detect new entrants to the media landscape.

source_name: WeBalkans.eu — EU funding opportunities and projects in Kosovo
why_relevant: EU-run communication platform aggregating IPA III, EU4 programmes, Digital Europe and Horizon participation for the Western Balkans; a fast index of programme names and acronyms to feed back into TED/F&T searches.
